thread:
maya: Heads-up — incoming request from Acme Payments: they want a low-latency, customer-tuned base model (no instruction tuning) quantized to int8, plus an optional 200k token long-context build for large legal docs. They care about p99 < 350ms on short requests and stable ROUGE for summaries.

owen: Ack. Do we have an int8 path validated for their model family? memory/gpu fit?

li: Quick update: int8 prototype exists for rwd-base-7b-family but longctx 200k needs chunked attention + offloading. For a 7B we can fit int8 on A10G with KV offload, but 200k will need disk-backed kv-cache or sharded KV across 2 GPUs. Latency will spike if we don't batch carefully.

maya: Important: customer explicitly asked for base (no instruct), but also wants deterministic outputs for reconciliation. Quantization nondeterminism flagged as a risk. Can we run a determinism sweep?

anita: I'll queue the determinism and QA tests. Proposal: run the following evals pre/post-quant: 1) summarization ROUGE-L on 1k legal samples, 2) QA exact-match on 500 reconciliation pairs, 3) perplexity drift on their fine-tune set. If any metric drops >3% we block.

eval-bot: queued eval job 5483: rwd-base-7b int8 vs fp16, datasets: acme-legal-summary (1k), acme-reconcile-qa (500). ETA ~ 2h.

owen: Also add latency microbench: 1-token and 64-token gen p50/p95/p99 with burst=1,10,50. We need the cost delta for int8 vs fp16. Could be the customer accepts slightly worse rouges for 2x cheaper inference.

li: Noted. I'm worried about model behavior: base models sometimes respond poorly to instruction-style prompts when customers add fronting system prompts for productization. Suggest we test both: base-only and lightweight instruction adapter (LoRA) as a fallback path. If base fails QA, roll in a tiny instruct adapter with minimal training on their examples.

maya: Good plan. Action items: 1) li — run GPU fit + offload feasibility and infra cost estimate (due EOD). 2) anita — run eval batch and flag regressions (ETA 2-3h). 3) owen — prepare perf microbench harness + cost calc (ETA EOD). 4) me — start contract note: non-determinism and fallback policies.

infra-bot: deploy job suggested: dedicated-pool:acme-payments, reserve: 2xA10G, fallback-route: hosted:fallback-7b-instruct, autoscale: on.

anita: Eval job finished preliminary: int8 shows 2.8% ROUGE-L drop on acme-legal-summary and EM -1.2% on QA. Perplexity drift +0.6. Latency p99 improved ~22%. Full logs uploaded: https://internal.redwood/evals/5483

maya: Thanks. Given threshold >3% block, this is borderline but acceptable if we document tradeoffs and offer instruct-adapter fallback. @owen can you run a quick smoke with LoRA adapter (10M params) to see if ROUGE recovers?

owen: Starting LoRA smoke now. If it recovers >1.5% we ship int8+adapter combo as the recommended config.

li: Also adding a note: longctx 200k build is an opt-in premium engineering project. I'll draft a checklist for long-context bring-up: kernel selection, KV offload sharding plan, checkpointing strategy, eval corpus for chunk boundary regressions. Will post in this thread when ready.

maya: Perfect. Keep updates here. If anyone makes changes to model-catalog or rollout policy, ping me. :thumbsup:
